ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Running into the exposed pillar is a collision image that masters turn into a warning and a verdict: the obstruction is standing in plain sight, yet the person meets it blindly.
EvidenceBody: Xuedou calls the Silla visitor a blind fellow who ran into the pillar. Dahui warns the assembly not to collide with it when the lamps go out and repeats the warning after a pillar saying; Caotang Shanqing asks where the collision occurs; Zhulang Chesheng makes avoiding the pillar one of his rules for the assembly; Zixian Jue invokes the blind collision while rejecting a stock appraisal; Yulin Tongxiu makes the stone base itself shout the phrase.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: An architectural mishap becomes a portable hall warning and a diagnosis delivered inside raised cases.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The corpus does not make every physical pillar symbolic, and the stored uses do not license one hidden psychological mechanism.

ComparedThings: the exact saying across different public occasions
DifferentThingTest.Reason: The witnesses change occasion and appraisal without changing the lexical unit.
